title: Integral parameter root projection and its nilpotent closed fibre
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $R$ a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, and $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in R$. Put $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, with closed inclusion $s:S\hookrightarrow U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For each positive integer $n$ prime to $p$ put
$$A_n=R[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{a,n}^n-t_a)_{a=1}^r.$$
Order these integers by divisibility, with transition $x_{a,n}\mapsto x_{a,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$, and put $A=\varinjlim_n A_n$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $q:T\to U$. Setting all roots to zero modulo $I$ defines $i:S\to T$. For a profinite set $P$ use the actual test scheme $X[P]=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(P,\mathbf Z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ and its projection [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Write $\pi_P:T[P]\to T$, $q_P=q\pi_P$, $B_P=T[P]\times_U S$, and $\rho_P:S[P]\to S$.
Each $A_n$ is finite free over $R$, with basis $\prod_a x_{a,n}^{e_a}$ for $0\leq e_a<n$. The morphism $q_P$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The map $i_P:S[P]\to T[P]$ factors through a surjective closed immersion $a_P:S[P]\hookrightarrow B_P$. On coordinate rings its quotient kills exactly the ideal generated by the images of all $x_{a,n}$, and this ideal consists of nilpotent elements. If $h_P:B_P\to T[P]$ and $q_{S,P}:B_P\to S$ are the projections, then $h_Pa_P=i_P$ and $q_{S,P}a_P=\rho_P$. These descriptions commute with arbitrary base change $R\to R'$, continuous maps of $P$, and further profinite parametrization, including simultaneous maps $Q\times P'\to P$. They include $r=0$, empty $P$, and the zero ring. The nil ideal is not asserted to have a uniform nilpotence exponent, and $B_P$ is not identified with $S[P]$ as a scheme.

proof.text: The indexing poset is nonempty since it contains $1$; $nm$ is a common multiple of $n,m$ and is prime to $p$. For $n\mid m$, substitution $x_{a,n}\mapsto x_{a,m}^{m/n}$ sends $x_{a,n}^n-t_a$ to zero, so gives a map of the presented quotient algebras. Composing for $n\mid m\mid l$ sends each root to $x_{a,l}^{(l/m)(m/n)}=x_{a,l}^{l/n}$ and fixes $R$, hence equals the direct transition. The polynomial and quotient universal properties and the colimit convention thus give the stated diagram and its compatible root classes in $A$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), elementary verification of the parameter-root algebra diagram

proof.text: For $R\ne0$, each $X^n-t_a$ is monic of degree $n$ since $n\geq1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-tensor-presentation] to these $r$ polynomials. Its finite tensor algebra $C_n$ has the basis of tensor powers with exponents $0\leq e_a<n$. Identify $C_n$ with $A_n$ as follows: evaluation gives $C_n\to A_n$ sending every distinguished root to $x_{a,n}$; conversely the inclusions of the one-variable factors give roots in $C_n$ satisfying the relations, so the polynomial quotient gives $A_n\to C_n$. Both composites fix $R$ and every root, hence are identities by the polynomial and tensor universal properties. The displayed basis therefore becomes precisely $\prod_a x_{a,n}^{e_a}$. Its index set is finite, including the singleton empty tuple when $r=0$, so $A_n$ is finite free. If $R=0$, all these algebras and their free modules are zero; the map from the finite direct sum of copies of the zero module $R$ is the unique isomorphism, so the same indexed basis assertion holds without using a polynomial degree in the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 03HW, lemma-massage-finite, displayed simultaneous monic quotient; finite tensor power basis supplied by the cited node

proof.text: Write $C_P=LC(P,\mathbf Z)$ and $D_P=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C_P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $T[P]=\operatorname{Spec}D_P$ and $q_P$ is induced by $R\to D_P$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. We prove this ring map integral in the next two steps, rather than infer integrality from weak etaleness of the parameter projection.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, tensor formula and projections

proof.text: Every locally constant integer function on compact $P$ has finite image: its open fibres cover $P$ and a finite subcover suffices. Fibres are also closed since their complements are unions of open fibres. Thus finitely many such functions are constant on a common finite clopen partition $F$. Its characteristic functions $e_v\in C_P$ satisfy $e_ve_w=0$ for $v\ne w$, $e_v^2=e_v$ and $\sum_v e_v=1$. These identities follow by evaluation at each point. The empty partition is used when $P=\varnothing$, in which case $C_P=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), elementary compactness argument for the profinite parameter ring

proof.text: For $z\in D_P$, write $z=\sum_{j=1}^s a_j\otimes f_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] each $a_j$ comes from a stage; a common multiple gives one stage $A_n$ for all $j$. Choose a common partition $F$ for the $f_j$ by step 4. There is a unital $R$-algebra map $A_n^F\to D_P$, $(b_v)_v\mapsto\sum_v\iota_n(b_v)\otimes e_v$: the characteristic-function identities prove multiplicativity and preservation of $1$. It contains $z$ in its image, by taking $b_v=\sum_j f_j(v)b_j$ for lifts $b_j\in A_n$. The source is a finite $R$-module, with spanning family the power basis of step 2 placed in each of the finitely many coordinates. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], the tuple mapping to $z$ satisfies a monic equation over $R$; applying the ring map gives that same monic equation for $z$. For $P=\varnothing$, $D_P=0$ and its sole element satisfies $X=0$. Hence $R\to D_P$ is integral, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-integral-ring-map-integral] proves $q_P$ integral.

source.place: Tag 00D6, lemma-directed-colimit; Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; morphisms.tex Tag 02K8, lemma-integral-local

proof.text: Set $\bar R=R/I$. The affine fibre-product formula gives $B_P=\operatorname{Spec}E_P$ with $E_P=D_P\otimes_R\bar R$, and $S[P]=\operatorname{Spec}F_P$ with $F_P=\bar R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C_P$. The compatible evaluations $A_n\to\bar R$, fixing base coefficients modulo $I$ and sending roots to zero, induce $\varepsilon:A\to\bar R$ by the colimit universal property. The tensor universal property gives a ring map $\varepsilon_P:E_P\to F_P$ with $(a\otimes f)\otimes\bar b\mapsto\bar b\varepsilon(a)\otimes f$. It has a section $\sigma_P:F_P\to E_P$, $\bar b\otimes f\mapsto(1\otimes f)\otimes\bar b$, so it is surjective. Its composite with $D_P\to E_P$ is exactly the coordinate map defining $i_P$. Consequently $a_P:=\operatorname{Spec}\varepsilon_P$ is a closed immersion and $h_Pa_P=i_P$.

Let $J_P\subset E_P$ be generated by every root image $x_{a,n}$. The map $\varepsilon_P$ kills these images. Conversely, modulo $J_P$ every element from every $A_n$ equals its constant coefficient modulo $I$: subtracting that coefficient leaves a sum of monomials divisible by a root. Every element of $A$ comes from a stage by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Expanding the finitely many pure tensors representing $y\in E_P$ therefore gives $y\equiv\sigma_P\varepsilon_P(y)\pmod{J_P}$. If $\varepsilon_P(y)=0$ this says $y\in J_P$. Thus $\ker\varepsilon_P=J_P$, and $E_P/J_P\cong F_P$.

source.place: Tag 00D6, lemma-directed-colimit; elementary quotient evaluation on polynomial generators

proof.text: Each generator $u=x_{a,n}$ of $J_P$ satisfies $u^n=t_a=0$ in $E_P$. An element $y\in J_P$ is a finite sum $\sum_{j=1}^s c_ju_j$. Choose $n_j\geq1$ with $u_j^{n_j}=0$. In the expansion of $y^N$ for $N=1+\sum_j(n_j-1)$, each term has some $u_j$ occurring at least $n_j$ times, and is zero; for the empty sum use $N=1$. Thus every element of $J_P$ is nilpotent. If $\mathfrak p$ is a prime ideal of $E_P$, $u^n=0\in\mathfrak p$ forces $u\in\mathfrak p$ by repeated primality, so $J_P\subseteq\mathfrak p$. The ideal $\mathfrak p/J_P$ is prime in $E_P/J_P$ (the prime condition follows immediately by lifting a product), and its inverse image is $\mathfrak p$. Therefore every point of $B_P$ lies in the image of $a_P$, proving surjectivity. No uniform exponent for $J_P$ was used.

source.place: Tags 00IL, definition-locally-nilpotent-ideal, and 0544, lemma-locally-nilpotent, binomial expansion; explicit prime-ideal argument

proof.text: On coordinate rings $q_{S,P}a_P$ sends $\bar b\in\bar R$ to $\bar b\otimes1\in F_P$, which is the map for $\rho_P$; hence these scheme maps agree. Apply [lem-sfb-root-tower-profinite-base-change] for $R\to R'$ and for the profinite parameters. Its root isomorphism fixes base coefficients and carries each named root to the corresponding root; the zero-root evaluations therefore agree on every coefficient and root, and then on the colimit. Pullback along $v:P'\to P$ replaces $f$ by $f\circ v$ in every displayed tensor formula and fixes roots. Thus it commutes with $\varepsilon_P$, $\sigma_P$ and the generating ideals. The same node identifies $(X[P'])[Q]$ with $X[P'\times Q]$ compatibly with projections. A simultaneous map $w:Q\times P'\to P$ uses $f\mapsto f\circ w$ in exactly the same formulas, so all asserted squares commute, including their composites and iterated parametrizations. This is equality of the actual ring maps and hence of the actual scheme maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), parameter-root base change and simultaneous parameter maps; explicit verification on coefficients, roots and locally constant functions

proof.text: For $r=0$ the root diagrams are constant $R$, $I=0$, $A=R$, and $J_P=0$; $a_P$ is the identity on $S[P]=B_P=U[P]$. Integrality still follows from the finite partition argument, now using $R^F$. Empty $P$ gives zero coordinate rings and empty schemes, so the closed immersion is surjective onto the empty fibre. If $R=0$ all schemes are empty. None of the kernel computations requires $\bar R$ reduced: its own nilpotents survive in $F_P$ and are not thereby in $J_P$. In particular the result asserts a nil kernel and a surjective closed immersion, not an isomorphism of $B_P$ with $S[P]$.

lean.statement: theorem integral_nil_fibre (hp : p.Prime) : (∀ n : TameRootOrder p, (∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r → Fin n.val) R (sncRootLevel t n.val), ∀ e : Fin r → Fin n.val, b e = ∏ i : Fin r, sncRootCoordinate t n.val i ^ (e i).val) ∧ Module.Free R (sncRootLevel t n.val) ∧ Module.Finite R (sncRootLevel t n.val)) ∧ ∀ P : Profinite.{u}, IsIntegralHom (qP p t P) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (stratumInclusion t) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (inclusion p t P) ∧ Surjective (inclusion p t P) ∧ Function.Surjective ((inclusion p t P).appTop).hom ∧ RingHom.ker ((inclusion p t P).appTop).hom = rootIdeal p t P ∧ (∀ y : Γ(fibre p t P, ⊤), y ∈ rootIdeal p t P → IsNilpotent y) ∧ inclusion p t P ≫ pullback.fst (qP p t P) (stratumInclusion t) = testMap (boundary p t) P ∧ inclusion p t P ≫ pullback.snd (qP p t P) (stratumInclusion t) = (test (stratumScheme t) P).hom
